Reading MAM-parsed-plus

The MAM-parsed-plus JSON files are a parsed representation of the Wikitext of the MAM dataset. This document covers:

  • File naming
  • Top-level structure and header metadata
  • Book39 entries (including good-ending data)
  • Chapter and verse structure
  • Template format (expanded representation)
  • Selected templates
  • Common templates in the verse-text column
  • Differences from plain format

File naming

File names (e.g. A1-Genesis.json) start with two characters that identify the book (in the “24 books” sense) and provide a standard ordering. The first character (sec_char) comes from the set ABCDEF and indicates the section of Tanakh. The second character (book24_char) comes from the set 12345AC and indicates the book within that section.

Files are named {sec_char}{book24_char}-{EnglishName}.json:

Prefix Section Books
A1–A5 Torah Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy
B1, B2, BA, BC Former Prophets Joshua, Judges, Samuel, Kings
C1–C3, CA Latter Prophets Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, The 12 Minor Prophets
D1–D3 Wisdom Psalms, Proverbs, Job
E1–E5 Five Scrolls Song of Songs, Ruth, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes, Esther
F1, FA, FC Late Books Daniel, Ezra-Nehemiah, Chronicles

When book24_char is A or C, the file is a composite book24, i.e. a book24 that contains sub-books (e.g. BA-Samuel contains both 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel). The letter B is not used in order to keep compatibility with a set of codes used for the 39-book system.

Top-level structure

{
  "header": {},
  "book39s": []
}

Header

Key Type Description
book24_names array A list that always has a single element: the name of this file’s book24.
sub_book_names object Maps each composite-book name to an ordered list of its sub-book names. Empty object for single-book files.
chapter_counts array One object per sub-book, each with book24_name, sub_book_name (null for non-composite books), and chapter_count.
he_to_int object Hebrew numeral → integer mapping for all chapter and verse keys in the file. 
"header": {
  "book24_names": ["ספר איוב"],
  "sub_book_names": {},
  "chapter_counts": [
    { "book24_name": "ספר איוב", "sub_book_name": null, "chapter_count": 42 }
  ],
  "he_to_int": {
    "א": 1,
    "ב": 2,
    "ג": 3,
    "...": "..."
  }
}

The he_to_int mapping allows consumers to navigate chapters and verses by integer without needing to implement Hebrew-numeral decoding. It is sorted by integer value and covers the union of all chapter and verse keys across all book39s in the file.

Book39 entry

{
  "book24_name": "ספר ישעיהו",
  "sub_book_name": null,
  "chapters": {},
  "good_ending_plus": null
}
Key Type Description
book24_name string For a non-composite book (book24=book39), this is the name of the book. For a sub-book, this is the name of the book24 to which this sub-book belongs.
sub_book_name string | null For a non-composite book (book24=book39), this is null. For a sub-book, this is the name of the sub-book.
chapters object Object keyed by Hebrew-numeral chapter numbers; values are chapter objects.
good_ending_plus object | null null for most books; an object for the 4 book39s that are sometimes presented with their next-to-last verse repeated.

Chapter structure

An object keyed by Hebrew-letter chapter numbers. A chapter with 22 verses has exactly 22 keys (א through כב), nothing more.

Verse structure

A 3-element array [C, D, E], with column details described below.

C column (index 0): Verse separator

The C column contains no "//"​ Wikitext line breaks from the source.

D column (index 1): Verse label

In plus, only the first verse of each chapter has the מ:פסוק template. All other verses have an empty []:

Job 1:1 (א — first verse of the chapter):

[
    ...,
    [{"tmpl_name": "מ:פסוק", "tmpl_params": {"1": "איוב", "2": "א", "3": "א", "סדר": "א"}}],
    ...
]

Job 1:2 (ב — any subsequent verse):

[
    ...,
    [],
    ...
]

E column (index 2): Verse text

Same mixed array of strings and template objects, but templates use the expanded format (see below).

Template format in plus

All templates in the plus format use the expanded representation:

{
  "tmpl_name": "קו\"כ",
  "tmpl_params": {"1": "את", "2": "אַ֠תָּ֠ה"}
}
Key Type Description
tmpl_name string Template name
tmpl_params object Parameters — present only when the template has params

tmpl_params keys

Numeric string keys "1", "2", … correspond to positional arguments, with any "2=" prefix already interpreted. Non-numeric keys (e.g. "ד", "ס", "סדר") represent named parameters like ד=... in the wikitext.

The tmpl_params object is absent only when the template has no parameters (e.g. פפ, סס, מ:פסק).

Template parameter values can be complex

Parameter values can themselves be strings, nested template objects, or arrays of mixed strings and template objects. For a visual overview of which templates nest inside which, see the plus template call graphs.

Accessing template parameters

Use tmpl_params directly with the string key:

def tmpl_param(tmpl, key):
    \"\"\"Get a template parameter by string key (e.g. '1', '2', 'ד').\"\"\"
    return tmpl['tmpl_params'][key]

Example — a word with a special letter inside a ketiv-qere inside a nusach:

{
  "tmpl_name": "נוסח",
  "tmpl_params": {
    "1": {
      "tmpl_name": "כו\"ק",
      "tmpl_params": {
        "1": {
          "tmpl_name": "מ:אות-מיוחדת-במילה",
          "tmpl_params": {
            "1": ["ו", {"tmpl_name": "מ:אות-ק", "tmpl_params": {"1": "ג"}}, "יש"],
            "2": "וגיש",
            "3": ".ג..",
            "4": "ק",
            "5": "ג/ק"
          }
        },
        "2": "וְג֣וּשׁ"
      }
    },
    "2": "=commentary text..."
  }
}

Selected templates

Each of the following templates has its own dedicated page:

  • Special letter marking — מ:אות-מיוחדת-במילה
  • Special ketiv-qere template — מ:כו"ק מיוחד
  • Targeted scroll-difference note — מ:הערה-2
  • Dual-trope text — מ:כפול

Common templates in the E (verse text) column

For authoritative English and Hebrew descriptions of every template, see the Templates tab of the MAM Google Sheet.

In plus format these templates use tmpl_name/tmpl_params format.

Documentation template (נוסח)

Its first parameter is the “target” — what is being documented. The second parameter contains the documentation (anomalous forms, variant readings, uncertain readings, etc.):

{"stmpl": "נוסח|וּבֵרְﬞכ֥וּ|2=א=וּבֵרֲכ֥וּ (חטף)"}

Ketiv-qere templates

Template Purpose
כו"ק Standard ketiv-qere. Param 1 = unpointed ketiv, param 2 = pointed qere.
קו"כ Post-maqaf ketiv-qere. Same parameters as כו"ק but used when the pair follows a maqaf.
מ:קו"כ-אם-2 Trivial ketiv-qere. Param 1 = pointed ketiv, param 2 = unpointed ketiv, param 3 = pointed qere.
כתיב ולא קרי Ketiv without qere. Single parameter = the ketiv.
קרי ולא כתיב Qere without ketiv. Single parameter = the qere.
מ:כו"ק מיוחד Special ketiv-qere. The required סוג= named parameter identifies the subtype. Nine subtypes.

Current values observed for optional סוג= in מ:קו"כ-אם-2:

  • אל"ף נחה באמצע תיבה ולא נקראת
  • כתיב ה"א בסיומת של חולם
  • כתיב הוא קרי היא
  • כתיב חסר יו"ד בסיומת של קמץ ואחריו וי"ו
  • כתיב נער קרי נערה

Example of standard ketiv-qere:

{"stmpl": "קו\"כ|את|אַ֠תָּ֠ה"}

Special letter templates

Template Purpose
מ:אות-ג Large letter. Marks a masoretically large letter. Parameter is the pointed letter.
מ:אות-ק Small letter. Marks a masoretically small letter. Parameter is the pointed letter.
מ:אות תלויה Suspended (hung) letter. Appears raised in the text.
מ:אות מנוקדת Dotted letter/word. Marks words with masoretic dots above/below.
מ:נו"ן הפוכה Reversed nun. The inverted nun mark (Unicode character).

Accent and cantillation templates

Template Purpose
מ:לגרמיה-2 Legarmeh. The vertical line ׀ as legarmeh (part of the word’s cantillation). Shares Unicode with paseq but differs in function.
מ:פסק Paseq. The vertical line ׀ as paseq in the narrow sense, i.e. paseq as distinct from legarmeh.
מ:מקף אפור Gray maqaf. A maqaf that is only implicit in the manuscript. Appears only in poetic verses.
מ:דחי Deḥi variation. Presents both stress-helped and non-stress-helped versions of a word.
מ:צינור Tsinnor variation. Presents both stress-helped and non-stress-helped versions of a word.
גלגל-2 Galgal. Distinguishes poetic from prose uses of Unicode YERAH BEN YOMO.
ירח בן יומו Yeraḥ ben yomo. Distinguishes prose from poetic uses of Unicode YERAH BEN YOMO.
אתנח הפוך Atnaḥ hafukh. Helps distinguish this accent from galgal/yeraḥ ben yomo.
מ:קמץ Qamats variation. Named params: ד= (grammatical) and ס= (Sephardic tradition).

Jerusalem spelling

Template Purpose
מ:ירושלם Handles the masoretic spelling of Jerusalem without yod. Two params (vowel and accent of lamed).
מ:ירושלמה Like מ:ירושלם but for the directional form “to Jerusalem” (4 cases).

Poetic form templates (ספרי אמת)

Template Purpose
ר1 Following stich on its own line, one indent. In 2 cases (Ps 70, 108) represents a closed parashah.
ר2 Following stich on its own line, two indents.
ר3 Following stich at line start, no indent.
ר4 New verse at line start, no indent.
ר0 Extra division point when a verse has an odd number of stiches, for even-column display.
פרשה-מרכז Centered title. For “titles” in Job and Proverbs. Parameter is the title text.

Many editions will choose to skip poetic formatting by treating פ0–פ4 as simple word spaces.

Footnote template

Template Purpose
מ:הערה Scroll-difference footnote (Torah and Esther only). Footnote markers appear within the text itself. Parameter is the footnote text.

Other templates

Template Purpose
פפ / סס Parashah petuchah / setumah (primarily in D column)
מ:סיום בטוב Good ending. Provides an unpointed version of the next-to-last verse. Used at the end of Lamentations, Ecclesiastes, Isaiah, and Malachi.
מ:טעם ומתג באות אחת Normalization-robust meteg for 10 cases where a below-accent and meteg share one letter.
מ:גרש ותלישא גדולה Combined geresh + telisha gedolah (2 words, 3 uses). No parameters.
מ:גרשיים ותלישא גדולה Combined gershayim + telisha gedolah (3 words, 4 uses). No parameters.

For the good_ending_plus JSON format and a worked example, see the good_ending_plus dedicated page.

Differences from plain format

Feature Plain Plus
Pseudo-verses “0” and “תתת” Present Removed
Custom XML tags (נוינקלוד etc.) Present Removed
Wikitext line breaks (“//”) Present in C column Removed
Named params not parsed unified with positional
D column (verse label) Every verse has מ:פסוק Only first verse of chapter
good_ending_plus Not present Added (at book39 level)
Hebrew numeral help Not present Added (he_to_int)
Words with special letters interrupted uninterrupted provided
{"tmpl": [...]} — parsed template trees Present Removed (replaced by tmpl_name/tmpl_params)
{"stmpl": "..."} — stringified templates Present Removed (replaced by tmpl_name/tmpl_params)
גלגל-2 — galgal accent annotation Present Removed (handled differently in plus)

Example of the stringified template format {"stmpl": "..."} (present in plain, replaced in plus):

{"stmpl": "קו\"כ|את|אַ֠תָּ֠ה"}
